Subject: OEM opportunity — embed Redwood into Compass

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Keystone's product team is excited about embedding inference directly into Compass (our enterprise search and insight UI).

High-level ask: we want a white-label/OEM option so Compass customers get the same seamless question-answering UX but processed by Redwood under our brand. Key requirements:
- Server-side SDK we can bundle with Compass server (Java/Node bridge)
- Option for outbound calls to Redwood Hosted OR a dedicated private deployment for larger customers
- Control over the displayed model name and branding (no Redwood logo in UI)
- SLA alignment for 99.9% availability for OEM customers on reserved capacity

Can you share what the product/commerce model looks like for OEMs and a term sheet we can review? Also looping in legal (copied) for early redlines on attribution / data residency.

Thanks,
Oliver

Quick answers up front:
- We support an OEM license for embedding our runtime behind partner branding (white-label).
- Two technical routes: lightweight API SDK (fast to integrate) or a private deployment package (VPC/air-gapped) for enterprise buyers.
- Branding: we can surface a partner name in responses; mandatory attribution is configurable depending on the contract tier.

I'm looping in Rishi (commercial lead) and Priyom (solutions engineer) to scope costs, runbooks, and the minimum viable integration (an integration sequence diagram attached).

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyom to validate the integration approach against Compass architecture.
2) Rishi to draft a preliminary term sheet outlining pricing bands (per-customer commits) + SLA add-ons.
3) Legal to flag any must-have clauses; we'll circulate a DocuSign term sheet once internal approvals are set.

I'll attach an initial term sheet draft for review — see redwood-oem-term-sheet-v1.pdf.

Hi all — I dug into Compass docs and sketched a minimal integration plan. Summary:

Integration options (pros/cons):
1) SDK + outbound Hosted calls
   - Pros: fastest to ship, central model updates, lower partner ops burden
   - Cons: partner cannot guarantee data locality unless they use private infra; attribution needs contractual waiver

2) Private deployment (VPC) per Keystone production cluster
   - Pros: full control over data residency, dedicated capacity (preferred for Fortune customers)
   - Cons: longer lead time, higher committed cost (we offer Dedicated pricing tiers)

Technical questions for Keystone:
- Does Compass run customer-specific tenant isolation (separate DB per customer) or a single multitenant DB?
- Expected QPS per customer for inference (median vs peak)?
- Will Keystone want to host the runtime or have Redwood manage a private instance?

I've attached an integration-sequence-diagram.png with the recommended flow: Compass -> Redwood SDK -> Request routing (hosted|private) -> Response. Also included a small CSV with sample non-prod env variables we typically exchange.

If you can share the QPS estimates, I can produce sizing for Dedicated pools and an initial cost estimate. Happy to set up an architecture workshop next week.

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: OEM opportunity — embed Redwood into Compass

Marissa / Team —

We reviewed the term sheet and have three immediate concerns:
1) Attribution: Keystone needs to remove any mandatory UI-level Redwood attribution for OEM customers.
2) Data residency & logging: For some regulated customers we must ensure full request-response logs stay in our VPC; what logs does Redwood collect/retain by default?
3) Indemnity / IP: Keystone needs clarity on model outputs and risk allocation for hallucinations.

Can you provide:
- A short statement on default telemetry we collect and an option to disable telemetry for private deployments.
- A revised attribution clause (we're proposing "Attribution optional for OEM customers with dedicated deployment").

Oliver, could you share the list of initial pilot customers so we can sanity-check regulatory constraints?

Regards,
Keystone Legal
legal@keystone.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Keystone Legal <legal@keystone.io>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@keystone.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2026 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OEM opportunity — embed Redwood into Compass

Thanks for the quick review. Short answers:

Telemetry & logs:
- Hosted (default): ephemeral telemetry for performance monitoring; request traces are retained for 30 days by default and can be exported.
- Private/Dedicated: telemetry can be disabled and we can provide a self-hosted agent that stores logs in your VPC only.

Attribution:
- We can support "Attribution optional for OEM customers with dedicated deployment" in the term sheet.

Indemnity / IP:
- We'll propose an output-liability cap aligned with committed spend and carve out gross negligence. We cannot accept open-ended indemnities for model outputs; propose an explicit section in the term sheet.

Next steps:
1) Rishi will circulate a revised term sheet (including updated attribution clause and telemetry options).
2) I will provide a DocuSign link for an NDA + pilot SOW once we align on pilots.
3) Tech workshop: Priyom proposes Tue, 24 Feb for architecture session — pls confirm.

Marissa
Head, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
